name: Compressed Random-Access Tree Framework
definition: A framework for compressing adaptive multiresolution hierarchies using a compact randomly-accessible tree structure. It uses fixed-rate encoding for both tree topology and data, replacing pointers with local offsets, using a forested mipmap structure, vector quantization of inter-level residuals, and efficient coding of partially defined data. Both offsets and codebook indices are stored as byte records.
summary: Compressed Random-Access Tree Framework enables fine-grain random queries for rendering by replacing pointers with local offsets and using fixed-rate encoding for topology and data.
